jobs.description:
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) is expanding its talented and international team to add to its cutting-edge quantum programme in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. At the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, we are running an international quantum computing programme, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, that drives research and innovations at multiple levels - from developing scalable quantum processor technologies to quantum algorithms and applications.  The long-term mission of the programme is to develop fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve life-science-relevant chemical and biological problems.

  The project 
 The position is centred on the development of integrated superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) embedded in controllable photonic circuits for the fully integrated processing of the emitted photons from silicon quantum emitters. The work will be performed as part of the Photonic Control and Readout team in NQCP, in close collaboration with the Theory & Simulation and the Materials engineering teams at NQCP and the Growth team at Quantum Foundry. These teams will support the efforts of the development and integration of SNSPDs in our photonic circuit.

  You will be collaborating closely with the other team members of the Photonic C&R team and – like the rest of the team - be generally involved in the projects related to the platform. A number of students will also be dedicated to the SNSPD projects. The nanofabrication is done at the DTU Nanolab – a 1,350 m² ISO 4–6 cleanroom with over 150 state-of-the-art tools, and one of the leading cleanrooms in Europe. Testing and integration of the SNSPDs will be done at the NQCP Photonics lab at the Niels Bohr Institute established in 2023. The lab contains a range of cryostats (mK to 4K) designed for optical fibre access, state-of-the-art electronics, commercial SNSPDs, etc.

  Responsibilities:

   	
• Taking the leading role in developing and integrating SNSPDs into our photonic circuits and establishing the electrical control circuit. 	
• Structuring the efforts on multiple projects, integrating experimental results in our database, and providing feedback to collaborating teams. 	
• Contributing to the other projects within the Photonics team. The projects span single photon sources and optical components like switches, cavities, etc. 	
• Teaching and supervision of students. 	
• Procurement, maintenance, and operation of scientific equipment.    

  We are looking for the following qualifications: 

   	
• PhD with postdoc experience in experimental physics, engineering, nanotechnologies, or related. 	
• Experience with SNSPDs fabrication and characterisation, quantum photonics, electronics, and cryogenic systems. 	
• Experience with control software and data logging – preferably in python. 	
• Good communication skills and a structured approach to work.   
 Assessment of applicants will primarily consider their level of documented, internationally competitive research. The ability to attract external funding will be considered together with outreach qualifications. Teaching qualifications are not mandatory but documented teaching qualifications and teaching experience will be considered.
 
 The position is also open as a postdoc. Please apply to the call corresponding to the position relevant for you. Only one of the positions will be filled.

  
 General criteria apply to the appointment of Assistant Professors at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, Innovation & societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.

  For Assistant professors: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5a_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-Assistant_professors.pdf.
 
 Why Us? 
 Joining NQCP now, you will get involved in a well-established and ambitious programme, which offers excellent opportunites to build a career in advancing quantum computing. We want to make Denmark a world leader in quantum research, and we hope to attract people from all over the world.  

  Life in Denmark is supported with strong social services (free universal healthcare, free/subsidised language courses, paid parental leave, subsidised day care institutions and excellent public schools). Our work culture is very egalitarian and prioritises work life balance. Dual career families are the norm, and workplaces offer flexibility to support everyone in having both an exciting career and good family time. Danish cities are known for having excellent infrastructure, for example through widespread bike path networks. We can also offer a thriving food-scene, excellent museums, and beautiful natural scenery. 
 
 Applicants are encouraged to read the University of Copenhagen's Guidance on the merit criterion Innovation and Societal Impact here.
  

  Further information on the Department can be found on the Niels Bohr Institute website. Inquiries about the position can be made to Stefano Paesani: stefano.paesani@nbi.ku.dk or Peter Granum: peter.granum@nbi.ku.dk.

   

  Start date is the 1st of February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.
 
 The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Terms of employment
 The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

   

  When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

   

  Please include

  1.                         Motivation letter (max. one page) 

  2.                         Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 

  3.                         Original PhD diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish.

  4.                         Publication list

jobs.occupation: Product Marketing Manager - B2B Software for Manufacturers
jobs.description:
Highlights:

• Fast-growing B2B software platform with established global reach is looking for our first marketing hire.

• We have a broad, multi-product offering for a narrow industry, and we don't fit into a single existing "category box" as defined today -- giving you a meaty challenge to work with.

• We have large customers and touch a lot of users (as a platform for managing global supply-chains), so your work will be "heard around the world"

• We are a small, efficient, get-stuff-done team. Looking for someone who things that's the way to go.

About Supplios

Manufacturers live or die by their supply base. Sourcing the wrong supplier, onboarding one slowly, failing to qualify one properly or losing track of a non-conformance can stop a production line and cost millions. Yet most manufacturers still run these relationships across email chains, spreadsheets and shared drives.

Supplios is a supplier collaboration platform for manufacturers in automotive and industrial sectors. We cover the full supplier relationship: sourcing, onboarding, qualification, day-to-day collaboration, compliance and supplier quality — with a modern cloud based platform that is easy for manufacturers to implement and operate. It is built specifically for the way automotive and industrial manufacturers actually work.

We are headquartered in central Copenhagen and already serve customers globally in our vertical, including some of the most demanding names in automotive. We have grown to this point almost entirely on product strength, domain credibility and word of mouth. We have done very little marketing.

That is where you come in.

The role

This is our first marketing hire.

You will own positioning, messaging and sales enablement for a platform that already has real customers, real reference stories and real competitive wins — but no one whose job it is to articulate any of it. There is no existing playbook to inherit, no legacy brand guidelines to work around, and no committee to navigate. There is a large amount of low-hanging fruit and a clear runway to make a visible commercial impact within your first few months.

You will work directly and closely with our co-founder and CEO, who continues to run product. He knows the product and the domain deeply; what he needs is a strong product marketing partner to turn that into sharp positioning, messaging that lands with procurement, quality and operations buyers, and material that makes the sales conversation easier.

This is a hands-on, execution-focused role. You will be writing the copy, building the deck and updating the website — not briefing an agency to do it.

We work together from our office in central Copenhagen. This is primarily an in-office role: at this stage, and in this role in particular, the close working relationship with management & sales is much easier to build in person.

What you will do

• Own positioning and messaging for the Supplios platform and its individual modules, and make it consistent across every touchpoint

• Translate technical capability into buyer-relevant value for distinct personas — sourcing and procurement leads, supplier quality engineers, quality directors, supply chain and operations management

• Build the sales enablement layer: pitch decks, one-pagers, battlecards, demo narratives, proposal content and objection handling

• Run competitive and market intelligence, and keep the team honest about where we genuinely win and where we do not

• Plan and execute go-to-market for new modules and major releases, in step with the product roadmap

• Develop customer proof — case studies, reference stories and use cases — from an installed base that has plenty to say

• Rebuild our website messaging and product pages so they reflect what we actually do and who we do it for

• Feed structured market and customer insight back into product decisions

What we are looking for

Essential

• Proven product marketing experience in B2B or enterprise software, with responsibility for positioning, messaging and sales enablement

• A demonstrable track record of translating complex, technical products into clear commercial value propositions

• Excellent written English

• Comfort operating without a marketing team, an established playbook or a large budget — you scope the work, then do it

• The temperament for a small, senior, fast-moving company: high ownership, low ceremony

Nice to have

• Domain knowledge in automotive, industrial manufacturing or supply chain. Genuinely a plus, not a requirement. We can teach the domain to the right marketer; we cannot teach product marketing to a domain expert.

• Experience marketing to enterprise buyers with long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles

• Experience as an early marketing hire at a growing B2B software company

Language

• English is the only important language for this position — we work in English, and so do our customers. Danish language skills are not required.

Why this role is worth your time

• First marketing hire, not the fifth. You define how this company talks about itself.

• A product that already works. Real global customers in a demanding vertical, and reference stories waiting to be told.

• Work directly with the CEO/founders. No layers between you and the decisions.

• Visible impact. In a company that has barely marketed, good product marketing shows up in the pipeline quickly.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note on why this role interests you to team@supplios.com. Work examples will help.

Apply by email

Send an email to team@supplios.com

Please include your CV / resume, and a brief note about why you're interested in the position.

Thanks!

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Predictive Human Digital Twins for Human-Centred Systems Engineering – DTU Construct
jobs.description:
Are you interested in human-centred engineering at the intersection of biomechanics, artificial intelligence, and systems engineering, and want to build a strong methodological profile, this PhD position offers a unique opportunity – including the chance to help shape a new research group from the start.

At DTU Construct, you will develop methods that turn generic musculoskeletal models into personalised Human Digital Twins – based on sparse wearable sensor data instead of costly laboratory measurements or medical imaging – and assess how reliably they predict how a person moves and interacts with technical systems such as collaborative robots or assistive devices. The project is part of building up a new research group in Human-Centred Design within the Human-Centred Systems Engineering activities at DTU Construct. As part of the DTU PhD programme, you will follow PhD-level courses and contribute to teaching.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall purpose will be to develop and validate methods for personalising biomechanical Human Digital Twins from sparse sensor data, combining physics-based and data-driven approaches and quantifying the gap between simulation and reality (sim2real).

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Develop methods for personalising musculoskeletal models from sparse multimodal sensor data.
• Combine physics-based and data-driven approaches for model calibration and prediction.
• Quantify and reduce the sim2real gap of Human Digital Twins.
• Plan and carry out experimental studies with human participants.
• Implement your methods in open, reusable software.
• Publish your results and collaborate with researchers at DTU and international partners.
We are looking for a motivated candidate with:

• An MSc in Biomedical or Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Engineering Design, or a related field.
• Solid programming skills (e.g. Python, MATLAB, C++).
• A background in simulation, optimisation, machine learning, sensor processing, or parameter estimation.
• A strong interest in computational modelling of humans and human-technology systems.
• Good communication skills in English and the ability to work both independently and in a team.
• Experience with musculoskeletal modelling (e.g. OpenSim, AnyBody, SCONE), motion analysis, or wearable sensing is an advantage.
• We do not expect you to master all of these areas – a solid foundation and the motivation to grow into the field matter most.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Jörg Miehling.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is 1 March 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Jörg Miehling, jormi@dtu.dk (please mention “PhD Position Inquiry” in your email subject).

You can read more about Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at www.construct.dtu.dk and the Section at www.construct.dtu.dk/sections/engineering-design-and-manufacturing-systems.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 2 December 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A copy of your BSc thesis (in pdf)
• A copy of your MSc thesis (in pdf)
• A copy of your scientific articles (if any) published so far (in pdf)
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Civil and Mechanical Engineering develops and utilises science and technical knowledge for the benefit of society and the sustainable development. We undertake research, education, innovation, and scientific advice of the highest quality within building design and processes, building construction and safety, building energy and technical services, solid mechanics, fluid mechanics, coastal and maritime engineering, materials technology, manufacturing engineering, engineering systems design, design for sustainability, and thermal energy.

The Section of Engineering Design and Manufacturing Systems (EDM) advances the design of intelligent, resilient, and sustainable products and manufacturing systems, integrating systems engineering, modular architectures, robust and bio-inspired design, and AI-enabled engineering.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

PhD in Physical AI for Adaptive Robot Manipulation
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Electrical and Computer Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
PhD in Physical AI for Adaptive Robot Manipulation

Research area and project description
Applications are invited for a fully funded three-year PhD position at the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Aarhus University. The position is part of STORM (Soft Tactile Memory for Safe Physical-AI Correction of Robotic Foundation Models), a new project funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF). The candidate will join the Adaptive & Agentic AI (A3) Lab, headed by Dr. Behzad Bozorgtabar (main supervisor), and will work closely with Professor Ahmad Rafsanjani and the SDU Soft Robotics group, who are developing the soft tactile skin.

Research vision
How can a robot foundation model use physical feedback to correct an action during execution? Models such as vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models let robots follow natural-language instructions, but they act on what they see rather than on what they feel. When a grasp begins to slip or a fragile object deforms, the camera view often looks fine until the damage is done. STORM gives robotic foundation models a sense of touch, so that a robot can notice when a manipulation is going wrong and correct itself safely while it acts.

PhD project
The candidate will develop the machine-learning core of STORM. The work spans three connected scientific questions, leaving room for the candidate to shape the specific algorithmic directions: (1) How can contact representations be learned from advanced tactile interfaces, including a soft-fluidic tactile skin developed at SDU? (2) How can predictive models forecast how contact states should evolve over short horizons under a policy's intended actions? (3) How can the mismatch between expected and felt contact drive parameter-efficient adaptation of pre-trained foundation policies while guaranteeing safety? Methods will be evaluated on public benchmark and real-world robotic setup, focusing on dexterous manipulation of fragile and unseen objects as well as safe human-robot interaction.

Environment
The project sits at the intersection of machine learning, Physical AI, robot foundation models (e.g., VLA and World-Action models), world models, tactile sensing, and adaptation algorithms—areas in which the A3 Lab publishes regularly at top-tier venues such as NeurIPS, ICLR, CVPR, and CoRL. The PhD includes a possible planned research stay at KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm, and close collaboration with the SDU team.

Qualifications and specific competences
This is a highly selective position; applicants are expected to meet the requirements below.

Education: A master’s degree (120 ECTS or equivalent) in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or a related quantitative field, completed or nearing completion before the start date.

Technical Skills: Advanced proficiency in Python and PyTorch, with hands-on experience training, fine-tuning, or adapting modern deep architecture such as Transformers, state-space/sequence models, and diffusion or flow-matching models.

Core Knowledge: A strong foundation in machine learning, deep learning, or computer vision, combined with a strong motivation to work on Physical AI, multimodal tactile sensing, world models, and online adaptation, etc.

Relevant Research Experience (one or more of the following is highly advantageous):
 
• Robot & Policy Learning: Imitation learning, behavior cloning, offline/model-based RL, or policy learning for manipulation (e.g., diffusion policies, Vision-Language-Action models, or World-Action models), as well as familiarity with manipulation benchmarks (e.g., LIBERO, CALVIN, or ManiSkill).
• World Models & Sequential Representation Learning: Self-supervised learning on temporal or multimodal sensor streams, action-conditioned video/dynamics prediction, latent world models, or uncertainty estimation.
• Model Adaptation & Post-Training: Test-time adaptation (TTA), continual/online learning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT/LoRA), or safe/constrained policy updates.
Hands-on Robotics: Prior experience with physical robot platforms, grippers, tactile/force sensors, and ROS 2 is an advantage, but not strictly required for candidates with an exceptional machine learning background. However, a strong willingness to work with physical hardware and run real-robot experiments is required.

Track Record: Evidence of strong research potential—such as a strong master’s thesis, open-source research code, or publications/submissions at leading ML, vision, or robotics venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, CoRL, RSS, ICRA)—is a strong advantage.

Attributes: A mindset for scientific rigor, reproducibility, and open-source contribution, the ability to collaborate across algorithmic AI and physical hardware teams, and excellent written and spoken English.

Title
New paradigm to disentangle hydrothermal stresses and assess regional agricultural vulnerability to drought-heatwave events

Research area and project description
The Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a three-year PhD position in remote sensing and knowledge-guided machine learning to assess agricultural vulnerability to drought and heatwaves. The expected starting date is 15 March 2027. The position is supported by the Sino-Danish Center for Education and Research (SDC) and involves collaboration with Chinese Academy of Sciences, including a research stay of 12 months.

Food security, climate change and biodiversity loss represent three major environmental sustainability challenges. The Center for Landscape Research in Sustainable Agricultural Futures (Land-CRAFT), established in June 2022, with expertise in biogeochemistry, agronomy and climate-impact research. This PhD project aims to develop a knowledge-guided machine-learning framework that combines remote sensing, field observations and process-based models to disentangle interacting stresses and assess agricultural vulnerability at regional scales. The research will distinguish the effects of soil water limitation, vapour pressure deficit, and temperature on crop productivity. The resulting knowledge and methods will support early warning, precision irrigation and agricultural climate-risk assessment.

The PhD student will work on three interconnected research tasks:
1. Develop an integrated observation framework for crop drought and heat responses. Combine thermal infrared, multispectral and hyperspectral remote sensing with soil moisture measurements, meteorological observations and field data to characterise crop responses across contrasting environmental conditions.
2. Disentangle the individual and interacting effects of water and heat stress. Quantify how soil-water availability, atmospheric demand and temperature influence crop functioning and productivity, and identify the conditions under which their interactions intensify crop stress.
3. Assess regional agricultural vulnerability to compound drought–heatwave events.
Scale the identified stress-response relationships from field observations to regional assessments, identifying vulnerability patterns, critical thresholds and hotspots.

SDC is a partnership between all eight Danish universities and the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (UCAS). It brings together Danish and Chinese research and education environments through collaborative research, joint supervision and international mobility. Participation offers the PhD student opportunities to gain research experience in both countries and build an international scientific network.

The student will be employed at Aarhus University, with Sheng Wang as the main supervisor with Kiril Manevski, Suxia Liu and Yongqiang Zhang as co-supervisors.
